title: GhJSON or GhPatch
description: Either a complete Grasshopper definition (a full GhJSON document) or an incremental edit to the definition already on the canvas (a ghpatch document). Which to emit: a ghpatch when the canvas state contains components YOU placed or edited on a previous successful turn (address them by instanceGuid); a full GhJSON document when nothing of yours is on the canvas yet — including the FIRST generation, even if the canvas state shows the user's own components (a full document places alongside them). Decide the document kind BEFORE you start writing, then output exactly one of the two structures — never draft one kind and switch mid-response. No prose, no markdown fences, no explanation. Only the raw JSON object.
rules: MODE: emit a ghpatch ("kind": "ghpatch") when the canvas state contains components from your previous successful turns, or when the user asks you to change their own existing components — you edit by instanceGuid copied from the canvas state. Emit a full GhJSON document when nothing you authored is on the canvas yet (first generation, or every prior submission was rejected) — even when the canvas state shows the user's own components; a full document places alongside them without touching them. If feedback says your submission was rejected before placement, the canvas is UNCHANGED: resubmit in the SAME document kind, fixing only what the feedback names. Never regenerate the whole graph when your components are already on the canvas.
name must exactly match the component's name in the Grasshopper library (case-sensitive), e.g. 'Addition', 'Construct Point', 'Number Slider'.

The grounding's installed-component list, when present, is the sole source of truth for which components may be placed: use only names it contains — plug-in components are allowed when listed, and unlisted components are not allowed however common. Without such a list, keep to native Grasshopper components. Do NOT use any scripting components (Python 3 Script, C# Script, GhPython, VB Script, or any other code-bearing node).

Every component needs a unique integer id; connections reference this id. In a ghpatch, existing components keep the ids shown in the canvas state, and every ADDED component gets a fresh id HIGHER than the highest id in the canvas state.

Every component needs a pivot 'X,Y'. Full document: lay the graph out left to right following data flow, about 150 units between stages (X) and 80 between parallel inputs (Y). Ghpatch: read the existing pivots in the canvas state and place additions so they continue the flow without overlapping.

connections has one entry per wire. Reference each endpoint by { id, paramIndex }: paramIndex is the parameter's zero-based position in the component's OUTPUT list (for 'from') or INPUT list (for 'to'), counting in the order shown in componentCatalog (or the component's installed order). paramName is optional and for readability only; the wire is matched by paramIndex. An input may receive SEVERAL wires — their items collect into a list in wire order, which is the idiomatic way to gather a few points or curves into one input (prefer this over Entwine/Merge for small fixed lists).

DATA TREES: for simple gathering, prefer wiring and list order (above) over tree edits. Reach for the parameterSettings modifiers (dataMapping graft/flatten, isSimplified, isReversed) on a specific port only to fix a branch-count mismatch — the classic case being pairing a list against another input one-to-one: graft the port whose items must each stand alone so a per-branch component sees one item per branch instead of matching one item against a whole list. Modifiers attach to a single input or output, not the whole component. In a FULL document, set them inside the component's inputSettings/outputSettings array entry for that parameter. In a ghpatch, MODIFY the component (do NOT remove and re-add it): inputSettings.byParameterName['<full parameter name>'].set = { "dataMapping": "graft" } (or isSimplified/isReversed/expression); clear one by setting it back ('dataMapping':'none', 'isSimplified':false).

Number Slider value uses the format 'default<min~max>', e.g. '5<0~10>', at componentState.extensions['gh.numberslider'].value. min must be strictly less than max. This is the most common mistake — do not use a plain number.

A slider is for values the user should tweak. To supply a FIXED constant (divide by 2, a unit vector, a base point), internalize it into the consuming input instead: inputSettings entry { "parameterName": "B", "internalizedData": { "{0}": { "{0}(0)": "number:2" } } }. Never add a slider whose min equals its max.
Give every Number Slider (and other input source) a nickName naming what it controls — 'Radius', 'Height' — never the default label.
Colours use the prefixed string 'argb:A,R,G,B', each channel 0-255.

GHPATCH: match every existing component you modify or remove by its instanceGuid copied exactly from the canvas state; never match by name. Copy the canvas state's base checksum verbatim into patch.base.checksum. Connections cannot be modified — remove the old wire and add the new one. Change slider values and panel text by MODIFYING the component's extensions in place, not by remove-and-re-add. Removing a component removes its wires too. Never re-emit components that are not being changed.

Components marked with the physalia.rhinoRef extension in the canvas state reference live geometry in the Rhino model. Wire FROM them by their id as data sources; never modify their values, remove them, or recreate them.
GHPATCH FEEDBACK: if some operations are reported as not applied, everything else DID land — resubmit a patch containing ONLY the corrected operations, regenerated against the current canvas state.

Inputs marked * in the grounding's component signatures are REQUIRED: wire them or internalize a value. A required input left empty produces nulls or no output, which silently breaks every component downstream.

FULL DOCUMENT: do not leave a non-source component's inputs all unwired; source components (Number Slider, Panel as input, Boolean Toggle, value params) legitimately have none. instanceGuid may be omitted (regenerated on placement). Omit document metadata and groups.

componentCatalog.description: Parameters for common Grasshopper components, listed in order. A parameter's paramIndex is its zero-based position in the inputs or outputs array below (first = 0). Components with no inputs are data sources. This is a convenience listing, not the set of allowed components — that set comes from the grounding's installed-component list.

componentNotes: Center Box: X/Y/Z are HALF-extents and the box is CENTERED on the base plane — it extends below Z=0 and measures twice each value. For a volume sitting ON the ground from a corner or with explicit extents, use Domain Box (Base plane + X/Y/Z Domains, e.g. Z domain 0 to height) instead.
Domain Box: takes Domains, not numbers — build each with Construct Domain. The go-to component for building masses that sit on the XY plane.
Boundary Surfaces: requires CLOSED planar curves. A PolyLine cap needs its Closed input internalized to boolean:true.

Entwine: grafts each input onto its own tree branch — a per-branch consumer like PolyLine then sees ONE point per branch and fails. To gather a few items into one list, wire them all into the same input instead.
Extrude: extrudes a curve or surface along a Direction VECTOR (build with Unit Z + Amplitude, or Vector XYZ) — a plain number is not a direction.
Loft / Ruled Surface: section curves must run in consistent directions and be listed in order; prefer Ruled Surface for exactly two rails.

fullDocument.description: A complete Grasshopper definition, placed on the canvas from scratch.

components.description: All Grasshopper components in the definition.

connections.description: Wires between component parameters. One entry per wire.

ghpatchDocument.description: An incremental edit to the definition already on the canvas.

patch.description: The patch body: what to add, modify, and remove.

base.description: The canvas state this patch was written against.

checksum.description: The base checksum, copied VERBATIM from the canvas state in the prompt.

add.description: Full component objects to place (fresh id above the canvas state's highest; omit instanceGuid).

remove.description: Components to delete, each matched by instanceGuid.

connections.description: Wire operations. Wires are immutable: move one by removing the old entry and adding the new.

groups.description: Group operations. Optional — most edits need none.

componentMatch.description: Identifies one existing component. Always use instanceGuid, copied exactly from the canvas state.

instanceGuid.description: The component's instanceGuid from the canvas state.

componentModify.description: An in-place edit: which component (match) and what changes. Include only the fields that change.

set.description: Component-type-specific values to overwrite, keyed by extension name — e.g. { "gh.numberslider": { "value": "5<0~50>" } }. Same encodings as the extensions definitions below.

inputSettings.description: Per-input setting changes keyed by the parameter's full name — mainly to change a data-tree modifier (dataMapping graft/flatten, isSimplified, isReversed, expression). e.g. { "byParameterName": { "Curve": { "set": { "dataMapping": "graft" } } } }.

outputSettings.description: Per-output setting changes keyed by the parameter's full name — mainly to change a data-tree modifier (dataMapping graft/flatten, isSimplified, isReversed, expression).

name.description: Component display name, exactly as it appears in the Grasshopper library, e.g. 'Addition', 'Number Slider', 'Sphere'.

id.description: Unique integer identifier, referenced by the connections array. In a ghpatch add, HIGHER than the highest id in the canvas state.

instanceGuid.description: Optional UUID v4. Regenerated on placement, so it may be omitted; omit it on ghpatch adds.

componentGuid.description: Optional component-type GUID. Leave this out — it is filled in from the live library. Do not invent a value.

nickName.description: On-canvas label. Set it on every input source — most importantly a Number Slider — to name what it controls (e.g. 'Radius', 'Height').

inputSettings.description: Optional per-input parameter settings. Only needed to change a parameter's behaviour; omit otherwise.

outputSettings.description: Optional per-output parameter settings. Omit unless changing an output's behaviour.

pivot.description: Canvas position as 'X,Y' (numbers may be negative or decimal), e.g. '100,200'.

componentState.description: Optional UI state and component-type-specific values. Omit for standard components that need no special state.

selected.description: Whether the component is selected on the canvas.

hidden.description: Whether the component's preview is hidden.

extensions.description: Component-type-specific values, keyed by extension name. Use only the key that matches the component (e.g. a Number Slider uses 'gh.numberslider').

ext_numberslider.description: Number Slider state. Used on a component whose name is 'Number Slider'.

value.description: Slider value as 'default<min~max>'. The default sits between min and max, and min must be strictly less than max (Grasshopper widens a zero-width range itself). To supply a fixed constant, prefer internalizing a value into the consuming input over pinning a slider. Decimal places set the slider's precision.

ext_panel.description: Panel state. A Panel with no input wire shows its own static 'text'; a Panel wired from upstream displays that data.

multiline.description: Whether text wraps onto multiple lines.

wrap.description: Whether text wraps within the panel width.

corners.description: Exactly three corner offsets 'x,y' relative to the pivot: [A, B, D]. The fourth corner is derived as B + D - A.

parameterSettings.description: Settings for a single input or output parameter. Only include the fields you need to change.

dataMapping.description: Data-tree mapping applied to THIS port (input or output). 'graft' moves every item onto its own branch — use it to pair a list one-to-one against another input so components cross-reference item-by-item instead of matching a single item against a whole list. 'flatten' collapses all branches into one flat list — use it when a downstream component needs a single list, not a tree. 'none' (the default) leaves the data structure unchanged; omit the field unless you are changing it.

expression.description: A per-item expression that transforms the port's values before they flow on, using 'x' for the incoming value (e.g. 'x*2', 'x+1'). Prefer a real component (Multiplication, Addition) for anything a reader should see; reserve this for a small inline tweak.

isReversed.description: Reverse the item order within each branch of this port.

isSimplified.description: Simplify the port's data tree, trimming path nesting shared by every branch — use when upstream grafting left the tree deeper than a downstream component expects.

isReparameterized.description: Reparameterize an incoming curve/surface domain to 0..1, so parameters along it read as fractions of its length rather than absolute values.

internalizedData.description: Persistent data internalized into an INPUT parameter of a component you are adding — the way to supply a fixed constant without creating a slider. The enclosing parameterName MUST be the parameter's FULL name exactly as listed in the grounding's component signatures (e.g. 'Closed', 'Origin'), never a one-letter canvas label ('C', 'O') — a wrong name silently applies nothing. A single value is {"{0}": {"{0}(0)": "number:2"}}; the inner value is a type-prefixed string such as 'number:2', 'integer:5', 'boolean:true', 'text:hello', 'pointXYZ:0,0,0', 'vectorXYZ:0,0,1'. A wired input IGNORES internalized data entirely — when you add a wire, never clear or modify the old internalized value; just add the wire. Never copy internalizedData from components marked physalia.rhinoRef.

connection.description: A single wire from a source output to a target input.

connectionEndpoint.description: One end of a wire. 'id' selects the component; 'paramIndex' selects the parameter.

paramIndex.description: Zero-based position of the parameter within the component's OUTPUT list (for 'from') or INPUT list (for 'to'). This is how the wire is matched; always include it.

paramName.description: Optional human-readable parameter label. For readability only; matching uses paramIndex.
